completion_data.completion_summary: Reproduced every verification command in the research report (correcting one genuine count defect), rendered the report's six recommendations as a 5-proposal backlog-reconciled packet, and bridged every actionable finding into issues.jsonl, all while editing nothing under FormalSystem/ and filing no task. Surfaced a live user priority ruling demoting the entire L^open transfer programme via user_decision.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan anticipates a single static foreign dirty file (another concurrent task's uncommitted modification) as the tree-movement risk to pin against, the real foreign state can instead be dynamic -- committing, then continuing to edit, multiple times during one dispatch. Treat it as a timeline of observations (each with HEAD + git status --porcelain, attributed to the concurrent task) rather than forcing it into a single static pin; reinterpret any downstream verification criterion that assumed a static baseline as testing the dispatch's own non-interference (nothing staged/reverted/committed by this task) rather than literal byte-identical output.

When auditing a report's grep-based existence/count claims for reproducibility, re-run against both the report's original pinned commit (via git show <pin>:<path> for files confirmed unchanged since) and the current committed state, and separately exclude any live-uncommitted edits by another writer. This distinguishes a genuine authoring-time error (count was already wrong at the pin) from pure tree movement (count changed because time passed), which determines whether the report body should be corrected or merely annotated with a tree-state note.

audit-task-proposals.sh verdicts against a dense, related-topic corpus are overwhelmingly scope-blind (no file_scope on the comparison target) or purely semantic (duplicate-of-open/subset-of-open/covered-by-closed with shared_paths: null). Collapse both categories to counts in a rendered proposal packet and surface only the shared_paths-backed verdicts individually -- those are the mechanically real overlaps, and rendering every purely-semantic match individually buries real signal in noise without added evidentiary value.

user_decision.question: A user priority ruling (specs/ROADMAP.md commit d863cb374, 2026-11-05) demotes the entire L^open transfer programme -- the subject of this ledger task and of all 5 surviving proposals (T1-T5) in proposals.json/proposals.md -- to a secondary line of investigation behind L-plus completeness/decidability. Six existing tasks in the same programme (860, 869, 873, 874, 875, 876) already carry this demotion annotation. Should T1-T5 be filed now (carrying the same demotion annotation, off both critical paths) alongside the other six, or should filing be deferred entirely until the L-plus critical path clears?
options: File T1-T5 now, each annotated with the same demotion ruling already applied to 860/869/873/874/875/876 -- keeps the backlog complete and ready to dispatch once priorities shift back

Defer filing all of T1-T5 entirely for now -- do not add more off-critical-path backlog while L-plus work is the active priority; proposals.md and the report remain available to re-derive the packet later with no information lost
user_decision.recommended: Defer filing all of T1-T5 entirely for now -- do not add more off-critical-path backlog while L-plus work is the active priority; proposals.md and the report remain available to re-derive the packet later with no information lost
